technical_and_design_decisions: Treat the increment as maintenance and enhancement work in an existing Spring-based codebase, preserving established module boundaries, APIs, test conventions, and build tooling.
Document BOM templates with practical examples showing dynamic inclusion of external libraries, version management, and any relevant Maven or Gradle usage already supported by the project.
Implement SPI integration coverage using the existing integration-test framework and CI-compatible service or mock infrastructure rather than introducing a new test platform.
Implement unit coverage with isolated mocks and fixtures for Lattice and YARN SPI behavior, reserving integration tests for protocol, wiring, and environment-dependent behavior.

Investigate the shutdown defect by reproducing the supplied JDBC-to-HDFS stream definition, then correct lifecycle, parsing, or resource-handling behavior with the smallest backward-compatible change.
Support multiple binder connection factories through explicit binder-specific configuration and selection, while retaining current single-binder configuration as the default behavior.
Add regression tests for the shutdown issue and focused unit/integration tests for multi-binder routing, connection-factory selection, and backward compatibility.
Use Java 17-compatible implementation and test code, consistent with the stated Spring Framework baseline.
assumptions: The existing source repository, build, test, and CI configuration are available and buildable without major environmental repair.
The placeholders Lattice, CC, YARN, container, and s-c-s refer to existing project components whose SPI implementations and current test conventions can be inspected in the repository.
Required external systems for integration testing are available through existing test containers, mocks, emulators, or shared CI services; provisioning a new production-like cluster is out of scope.
The BOM documentation is a repository documentation change and does not require a new dependency-management feature.
The shutdown issue can be reproduced with a representative JDBC stream and does not require access to the specific historical Oracle and HDFS environments.
The multiple-binder-connection-factory requirement can be delivered without breaking existing public configuration properties or requiring migration of existing applications.
Code review, release approval, and waiting time are excluded; implementation, local validation, test execution, and documentation updates are included.
Effort is estimated for one developer and includes reasonable investigation and debugging time for an unfamiliar or partially documented codebase.

activities.activity_description: Inspect relevant modules, SPI implementations, existing unit and integration tests, build profiles, CI jobs, configuration mechanisms, and the referenced issue behavior. Establish the implementation and test scope for all eight user stories.

Write and format reference documentation explaining BOM templates, dynamic external-library inclusion, version management, prerequisites, and representative usage examples. Validate examples against the existing build configuration.
Extend or configure common integration-test fixtures, lifecycle setup, test data, service endpoints, cleanup, and CI execution support needed by the Lattice, CC, and YARN SPI test suites.

Add end-to-end or component integration scenarios for the Lattice SPI, including normal operation, configuration, lifecycle behavior, error handling, cleanup, and assertions suitable for continuous CI execution.
Add CI-executable integration scenarios for the CC SPI covering initialization, representative operations, configuration propagation, failure behavior, and resource cleanup.
Add integration scenarios for YARN SPI deployment or execution flows, status and lifecycle transitions, configuration handling, failure paths, and cleanup in the available test environment.

Create isolated unit tests for Lattice SPI adapters, validation, mapping, lifecycle logic, error handling, and interactions with mocked dependencies. Include edge cases identified during reconnaissance.
Create isolated unit tests for YARN SPI orchestration, state handling, configuration conversion, validation, failure handling, and dependency interactions using existing mocking conventions.

activities.activity_name: Container shutdown defect reproduction and diagnosis
activities.activity_description: Reproduce the supplied JDBC-to-HDFS stream shutdown failure or a representative equivalent, trace administrative shutdown through parsing, deployment, and resource lifecycle code, and identify the root cause.

Implement the minimal backward-compatible correction so the affected stream can be stopped from the Admin UI, including safe handling of JDBC arguments, deployment state, and resource cleanup as indicated by diagnosis.
Add automated regression coverage for the supplied stream definition and related shutdown paths, then run existing container lifecycle tests to check for regressions in other stream types.

activities.activity_name: Multiple binder connection-factory design and implementation
activities.activity_description: Design and implement configuration and runtime selection for more than one binder connection factory, including binder-specific consumer and producer association, factory lookup, validation, lifecycle management, and preservation of the existing default behavior.

Add unit and integration-level tests for multiple connection factories, mixed consume and publish destinations, explicit binder selection, missing or invalid configuration, isolation, and backward-compatible single-factory operation.

activities.activity_name: Final validation, CI integration, and documentation updates
activities.activity_description: Run the complete relevant build and test suites, resolve test or portability issues, verify CI configuration and test stability, update configuration or user documentation for the implemented behavior, and prepare the increment for delivery.
